evidence.quote: | Ready, Some books when not (books.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && books.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && books.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && books.Payments.IsEmpty) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The transfer file's format, its checks and the order of its refusals live in Summa.Storage.Transfer (Tier 2). The rules about which pages accept a transfer (GitHub vs local, Settings only, only into new books) and the import itself live in the Summa.Web.Engine transitions (Tier 2). The Tier 3 wire only maps the three kernel events to engine messages, and app/index.html only binds the view values and events. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code decides a domain rule.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The time comes in with the message (ctx.Now), and the file name uses the model's business date. The download goes out as an OfferDownload effect and the save as the existing SaveBooks effect through `save`, so the Tier 4 kernel carries both out. Transfer.fs uses an in-memory MemoryStream/Utf8JsonWriter and JsonDocument only to build and parse text. That is not I/O, so no effect is performed or read below Tier 4. (Using System.IO/System.Text.Json symbols in Tier 2 may conflict with the instance's symbol rule ARC-SYM-01, but it is not an effect-flow failure.)

evidence.quote: | _, _, false -> { model with Error = Some "This browser cannot offer downloads here." }, []
| _ -> { model with Error = Some "This browser cannot offer downloads here." }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The main facts each have one definition that every use references. Schema and Version are literals, the classification comes from Exports.Classification, the data version from Exports.dataVersion, the snapshot from LocalSnapshot.encode/decode, and the 'not a transfer file' sentence is one private value. Some facts are restated, but the copies agree: the existing 'cannot offer downloads' sentence is copied as a new literal instead of shared, the 'yyyy-MM-dd' date format appears as a literal twice in the new engine code, and the 'new books' emptiness predicate is written inline in the transition.

evidence.quote: if version = 2 && contentsOf root <> Some(contents restored.Books) then

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The counting rule (customers, issued invoices, recorded payments), the version 2 contents check and the version handling live in Summa.Storage.Transfer (Tier 2). The preview in the Tier 2 engine view calls Transfer.read and Transfer.contents rather than recounting or re-checking anything. Tier 4 (app/index.html) only binds booksTransferPreview, and Tier 3 is not touched.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added. The preview is a pure projection of the pasted text in the view, and the contents check is pure parsing and comparison in Tier 2.

evidence.quote: if version = 2 && contentsOf root <> Some(contents restored.Books) then
| Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The contents count has one authority, Transfer.contents, used by export, read and the preview. The version 2 refusal sentence is defined once. But read restates the current version number as bare literals (`version = 1 || version = 2`, `version = 2`) instead of referencing the Version literal. The engine also copies the 'This file cannot be imported: ' prefix from the import transition and the 'yyyy-MM-dd' format literal again. These copies agree today, but each could drift.
